title: improv·artist · atmospheric (Mark Rothko)
mutation_directive: improv artist: atmospheric via Mark Rothko

improv_extras.practice: color fields that vibrate; contemplative; soft rectangles bleeding into ground

v1.feedback: Strong conceptual execution: differential growth silently evolves to partition space into Y-bands that become Rothko's horizontal color fields, with particles drifting and fading at edges for bleeding rectangles. The palette (ochre/sienna/charcoal) reads correctly and particles occupy substantial frame. However, the breathing motion feels timid (0.08/0.05 drift) — Rothko's fields *vibrate* optically, so increase the per-band color temperature oscillation or add subtle noise to vCol in the vertex shader to create that optical buzz between adjacencies. The edge fade logic (smoothstep on abs(p.x)) could be sharper to read as distinct rectangles rather than one soft gradient.

v2.feedback: The differential growth curve exists but is never rendered — it only partitions Y-space to assign particles to color bands, which is conceptually clever but visually reads as generic horizontal stripes with drift noise, not Rothko's signature bleeding-edge rectangles. The 'vibrating' color fields are just sinusoidal RGB noise (±0.08) on every particle, creating visual static rather than optical resonance between stable planes. To execute the brief: render the actual grown silhouette as translucent layered quads that partition the canvas into 2-3 soft-edged horizontal zones, skip the particle cloud entirely, and let the differential growth's organic boundary become the bleeding edge between fields.
